content:
I would like a local version of radar for FLT so I can see how PRs to it change compilation time. I have a decent unix machine, and FLT only takes a few minutes to compile on it (FLT is nowhere near as big as mathlib). Is this the sort of thing I can run locally?

(Background: there are a bunch of definitions and theorems in FLT which are very suitable for mathlib but recently have been slow to compile especially after v4.29. We feel like we're close to solving these problems but it would be nice to have tooling which confirms we're going in the right direction).
If you want, I can add FLT to our radar instance with a setup similar to cslib.
It would also be great to have a radar instance for Iris-Lean. Can we (as the Iris-Lean maintainers) self-host this somewhere or should this also be added to the official radar instance?

Joscha Mennicken said:

If you want, I can add FLT to our radar instance with a setup similar to cslib.

I'm not familiar with the cslib set-up. At the end of the day the thing I would really like would be to say things like "see what has happened to FLT after this PR" (which might well be a mathlib bump PR) and the thing which would be nice would be a warning if any PR made compile time go up a serious amount (I guess this is what cslib has?)
Cslib's setup is similar to mathlib (just without the open-mathlib and lint benchmarks), which sounds like it should fulfill your criteria.

Michael Sammler said:

It would also be great to have a radar instance for Iris-Lean. Can we (as the Iris-Lean maintainers) self-host this somewhere or should this also be added to the official radar instance?

I can also add you to our instance.

Joscha Mennicken said:

I can also add you to our instance.

This would be great! What would you need for this? (cc @Markus de Medeiros and @Zongyuan Liu )
I'm currently going through the existing bench suites and refactoring them to be more similar to each other again; they diverged a bit over time. I'll let you know once I need your attention again.

@Kevin Buzzard I've PRed a bench suite in FLT#1112, though (as explained in the PR), radar should already be usable without it. I've also queued the most recent commits, so radar gets a bit of data to calibrate its noise detection on. If its significance detection is still not working properly next week, manual tweaks may be required.
Thanks! FLT#1100 would be an interesting one to benchmark. I think that this one might be one of the breakthroughs we've been looking for for a while.
You should be able to just !bench it (though you'll need to wait a day or two for proper noise detection, so you may need to resort to sorting by % changed manually for now)

@Michael Sammler Since Iris-Lean is set up differently from the other mathlib-based radar-ified projects, there's multiple ways to proceed. The simplest solution would probably be for me to set up benchmarks just for the Iris subdirectory. You could also try setting up your own bench suite that's more specifically tailored to your repo.
That would be great. For the time being, only the Iris directory will contain code we expect to be slow.
If there's anything we can do on our end to help you out, let us know
I've PRed iris-lean#512 (see PR description for more details), should be ready to merge. I've also queued the most recent few commits, to collect a bit of data.
Perfect, thank you! I just merged the PR.
